title: Optimising the metric, not the forecast: code and data release
description:
Code and data for the manuscript Optimising the metric, not the forecast: how an automated loop exploits a grid-code accuracy score. Three years of an automated post-processing loop on a provincial Chinese wind fleet: 106 runs, 5,360 iterations, 1,202 accepted code edits. The loop raised the grid-code accuracy score by 1.02 points; the gain survived both holdout designs and transfer outside each pipeline's search set, but not a change of loss (capacity-normalised squared error worsened in 64% of runs). Three experiments locate the cause: an exact decomposition attributes +1.44 of the +0.90-point change to intervals inside the floored region and -0.54 to the rest; a single multiplicative constant gains 4.19 points where the loop gained 1.10; and re-running the loop with the floor removed from the objective collapses its gain to 0.05 points.

The archive contains the artefacts of all 138 runs (106 floored, 32 floor-free), the result tables behind Tables 2-10, the scripts that produce every printed number and Figures 2-6, a verification script that re-checks 142 printed values, and the search loop itself. The metered output and forecast series are confidential under a data-sharing agreement with the provincial system operator and are not included; no de-identified sample is included and requests for access cannot be granted. Code is released under MIT; result tables and run artefacts are released under CC BY 4.0.
